conventions: לְמַעַן takes the whole English compound the ASV writes for it — 'For ... sakes' (v8, discontinuous around its object) and 'For the sake of' (v9) — headed on sake(s) under rule 24; the 'of' closing 'For the sake of' is the compound's own and never the following construct noun's, which keeps only its supplied 'the' (rule 29) while its rectum takes its own 'of' (rule 19).
report: Read all 11 candidate lemmas end to end and the full dump of nine verses; no construction is analysed two ways without the ASV licensing the difference.

הוּא Sp2fs thee/thy, לְ of/for/unto/To, בְּ within/when, בַּיִת with or without a supplied 'unto', שָׁלוֹם bare vs 'the peace' (construct), כִּסֵּא 'thrones'/'The thrones', הָיָה 'are'/'be': each follows what the ASV wrote in that verse.

לְמַעַן is consistent across v8 and v9: the whole compound ('For ... sakes', 'For the sake of') goes to the preposition headed on sake(s), and the 'of' of v9 is the compound's, not the house's; the following construct chains take their own supplied 'the' and 'of' under rules 29 and 19.

The two fusions with שָׁם (v4 שֶׁ+שָׁם → 'Whither', v5 שָׁם+directive he → 'there') and the two added connectives (v4 appositional 'even' with no marker, v7 'And' with no waw) are all correctly placed and consistent with each other.
v1 'unto the house' (rule 33 on the bare directional construct) vs v6 'Pray for' (rule 44 on the verb reaching its bare object) are different constructions, not a split.
BSB disagreements (v3 reflexive לְ and its suffix, v8 second possessive suffix rendered by one 'my') are documented convention differences, not errors.
Nothing here generalises beyond the contract as it stands; no promotion or amendment.
